Rate your proficiency in identifying training needs (1–10).

Rate your proficiency in workforce planning (1–10).

What is a primary goal of talent acquisition?

options.A: Identify and attract candidates who fit the role and organizational needs
options.B: Hire as many applicants as possible
options.D: Guarantee every candidate accepts an offer

questions.question: A role requires a specialized technical skill. Which sourcing approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Target channels and communities where candidates with that skill are likely to be found
options.B: Post only on unrelated general-interest sites
options.C: Contact every applicant regardless of fit

questions.question: Before recruiting for a role, why should the hiring team clarify job requirements?

options.A: To define the capabilities and responsibilities needed for effective screening and selection
options.B: To guarantee a candidate accepts the offer
options.C: To reduce the need for onboarding
options.D: To avoid speaking with the hiring manager

questions.question: A recruiter receives 500 applications for a role. What is a sound first step?

options.A: Apply consistent job-related screening criteria
options.C: Choose candidates based on profile-photo quality

questions.question: Why is a structured recruitment process valuable?

options.A: It improves consistency and helps candidates be evaluated against relevant criteria

questions.question: A sourcing channel produces many applicants but very few qualified candidates. What should be investigated?

options.A: Candidate quality and channel relevance

questions.question: What is a candidate pipeline?

options.A: A tracked set of candidates moving through recruitment stages

questions.question: A candidate meets every required qualification but has not worked in the exact same industry. What should the recruiter consider?

options.A: Transferable skills and evidence against the actual role requirements

questions.question: Why is timely communication important during recruitment?

options.A: It supports a clearer and more professional candidate experience
options.C: It removes the need for interviews

questions.question: A student claims hands-on recruiting experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: How they sourced, screened, evaluated, coordinated, and tracked candidates for a real role
options.B: Only which recruitment platform they used

questions.question: What is a structured interview?

options.A: An interview using consistent job-related questions and evaluation criteria
options.C: An informal conversation with unrelated questions
options.D: An interview based only on intuition

questions.question: Which interview question is more directly job-related?

options.A: Describe a situation where you solved a difficult problem relevant to this role.
options.D: Where would you travel if you had free time?

questions.question: Why use the same core questions across candidates for the same role?

options.A: To improve consistency of evaluation

questions.question: A candidate gives a strong interview answer but lacks a mandatory technical requirement. What should the hiring team do?

options.A: Evaluate the candidate against the defined role requirements
options.B: Ignore the requirement because the interview was good
options.C: Change the requirement after the interview automatically

questions.question: What is a behavioral interview question generally designed to assess?

options.A: How a candidate handled a past situation or behavior relevant to the role

questions.question: An interviewer writes, "I just liked the candidate." What is missing?

options.A: Specific job-related evidence and structured evaluation criteria

questions.question: Why are scoring rubrics useful during interviews?

options.A: They make evaluation more consistent against defined criteria
options.B: They guarantee the best candidate every time

questions.question: A hiring panel gives widely different ratings because each person uses different standards. What should be improved?

options.A: Shared evaluation criteria and interviewer calibration

questions.question: A candidate has strong evidence for four of five required capabilities. What should the team do?

options.A: Identify whether the fifth capability is essential and assess the candidate against the actual requirement
options.C: Automatically reject every candidate with one gap

questions.question: A student claims substantial interviewing experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: How they structured questions, evaluated responses, recorded evidence, and supported a selection decision

questions.question: An employee raises a workplace complaint. What should HR generally do first?

options.A: Listen, document the concern, and follow the appropriate process
options.D: Publicly discuss it with the team

questions.question: Two employees have conflicting accounts of an incident. What is an appropriate first step?

options.A: Gather relevant facts and hear the involved parties before reaching a conclusion
options.B: Automatically trust the more senior employee

questions.question: Why is documentation important in employee-relations cases?

options.A: It creates a record of relevant facts, actions, and decisions
options.B: It guarantees one side is correct

questions.question: A disagreement between two employees is escalating. What is a productive HR approach?

options.A: Understand the issues, establish facts, and facilitate an appropriate resolution process

questions.question: What is an important consideration when handling sensitive employee information?

options.A: Limit access to people who have a legitimate need to know
options.B: Share it with the whole team

questions.question: A manager and employee disagree about performance expectations. What should HR encourage?

options.A: Clarification of expectations, evidence, and documented goals

questions.question: A workplace complaint involves several employees and similar concerns. What should HR consider?

options.A: Whether there is a broader process, policy, management, or culture issue
options.B: Treating every incident as unrelated automatically

questions.question: What is active listening useful for in conflict resolution?

options.A: Help clarify concerns and ensure each party is understood

questions.question: A manager wants to discipline an employee based only on a rumor. What should HR advise?

options.A: Establish relevant facts and follow the appropriate process before deciding

questions.question: A student claims practical employee-relations experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: How they handled a real issue, gathered information, documented it, protected confidentiality, and reached or supported a resolution
options.C: Only the number of employees involved

questions.question: What makes a performance goal more useful?

options.A: It is clear, relevant, measurable where appropriate, and connected to role expectations

questions.question: An employee repeatedly misses an agreed target. What should the manager first clarify?

options.A: The expectation, evidence, blockers, and support needed

questions.question: Why are regular performance conversations useful?

options.A: They allow progress, feedback, blockers, and expectations to be discussed before formal reviews
options.B: They eliminate the need for goals

questions.question: Effective performance feedback should focus primarily on:

options.A: Observable behavior, results, expectations, and improvement actions

questions.question: An engagement survey shows low scores around career growth. What should HR investigate?

options.A: Development opportunities, manager support, career paths, and employee expectations

questions.question: Why should engagement surveys be interpreted alongside other evidence?

options.A: Survey responses may need context from qualitative feedback, turnover, manager data, or other indicators

questions.question: An employee's output is low because required tools are unavailable. What should be addressed?

options.A: The operational blocker as well as the performance expectation
options.C: The goal should always remain unchanged

questions.question: What is a performance improvement plan generally intended to provide?

options.A: Clear expectations, support, timelines, and measures for improving performance
options.D: A way to remove job responsibilities

questions.question: A team has high workload and declining morale. What should HR and management consider?

options.A: Workload, staffing, priorities, management practices, and employee feedback
options.D: Measuring engagement once and doing nothing else

questions.question: A student claims substantial performance-management experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: How they set expectations, reviewed evidence, gave feedback, handled blockers, and tracked improvement

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a training-needs analysis?

options.A: Identify the gap between current capability and required performance
options.B: Schedule training without identifying a need

questions.question: Employees know a process but are not following it. What should L&D investigate before designing training?

options.A: Whether the issue is actually a knowledge or skill gap rather than a process or incentive problem

questions.question: A useful learning objective should describe:

options.A: What the learner should be able to do after the learning experience

questions.question: Training attendance is high but job performance does not change. What should be evaluated?

options.A: Whether learning transferred to the workplace and addressed the actual performance gap

questions.question: Why is practice important in skills training?

options.A: It gives learners an opportunity to apply the target behavior or skill
options.D: It reduces the need for feedback

questions.question: A technical team lacks a required capability for an upcoming project. What should L&D identify?

options.A: The exact capability gap, required proficiency, audience, and timeframe

questions.question: Why should training content reflect actual job tasks?

options.A: It improves relevance and the opportunity to transfer learning to work
options.C: It removes the need for evaluation

questions.question: What is a stronger measure of training effectiveness than attendance alone?

options.A: Evidence that learners can apply the required skill or behavior

questions.question: A course receives excellent satisfaction ratings but no improvement in performance. What does this show?

options.A: Positive participant reaction does not by itself prove transfer or business impact

questions.question: A student claims L&D experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: How they identified the need, designed the learning, delivered it, evaluated it, and assessed workplace impact
options.B: Only which learning platform they used

questions.question: What is HR analytics primarily used for?

options.A: Use workforce data to understand patterns and support HR or business decisions

questions.question: A company has 1,000 employees and 50 leave during a period. What is the simple turnover percentage for that period?
What is workforce planning intended to align?

options.A: Future workforce capacity and capability with organizational needs

questions.question: Why do organizations use compensation benchmarking?

options.A: To compare pay levels with relevant external or internal reference points
options.B: To guarantee every employee earns the same

questions.question: A company discovers similar roles have materially inconsistent pay without a clear explanation. What should HR investigate?

options.A: Role requirements, internal equity, market data, tenure, performance, and applicable policy

questions.question: What is a major purpose of employee onboarding?

options.A: Help new employees understand their role, tools, expectations, and organization

questions.question: A new employee has not received system access after one week. What should HR or the manager investigate?

options.A: The onboarding workflow and ownership for required access

questions.question: What is an HRIS primarily used for?

options.A: Store and manage structured employee and HR process information

questions.question: A business expects rapid growth but currently lacks enough employees with a critical skill. What should workforce planning consider?

options.A: Future demand, current capacity, skill gaps, hiring, development, and timing

questions.question: A student claims practical HR-analytics or workforce-planning experience. What should they be able to explain?

options.A: The data used, metric definitions, analysis, workforce question, assumptions, and decision supported by the findings
